candidate.description: Run only GGUF AOTriton prefill attention on one lazy event-linked nonblocking stream, with query/K/V preparation and post-attention work left on the caller stream.
candidate.current_default: off pending clean 128K and promotion gates
candidate.backend_scope: candidate is executable on gfx1100/gfx1151 by explicit selector; no backend package enables it automatically in this commit

red_green.red: tests/test_qwen35_gguf_aotriton_stream.py initially failed 3/3: no GGUF stream policy, runner bridge parameter, or resident bridge lifecycle.
red_green.green: The focused candidate plus gfx1151 backend and adjacent PARO bridge tests pass 20/20 + 2/2; targeted Ruff passes after excluding only pre-existing F401/F841 diagnostics in qwen35_gguf_runner.py.

correctness.protocol: Separate fresh processes for selector off and on; one shared-weight max-4K resident session per process; repeated token 9707; bulk WMMA prefill; exact comparison of sampled token, FP32 logits, FP32 hidden seed, all 30 Conv/GDN state pairs, and all 10 live BF16 K/V pairs.

fresh_process_focus.protocol: One discarded warmup plus three measured prefill-only runs in a fresh process per context/mode; 512 order off/on and 4K order on/off; cached builds; no decode. Worktree was intentionally dirty with the candidate, so these focus numbers are not a retained performance claim.

candidate_4k_profile.protocol: No warmup, one profiled prefill-only run; compared to the GPF-M2 complete baseline trace at 81e2f4b8.

invalid_same_session_observation.finding: Alternating off/on in one resident process measured flat because the first same-stream AOTriton warmup permanently contaminated the caller queue for later candidate legs. Queue-local persistence makes same-process interleaving invalid for this candidate; fresh process isolation is required.

decision.next: Commit the default-off implementation, then validate from a clean detached commit at 128K and run clean fresh-process 512/4K confirmation before adding the gfx1151 backend capability and publishing.
